question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $46u+14v=\text{gcd}(46,14).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}46 & = & 14\cdot 3 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 14 & = & 4\cdot 3 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 4 & = & 2\cdot 2 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(14,46)=2.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =46-14\cdot 3 \\ 2 & =14-4\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =14-4\cdot 3 \\  & =14-[46-14\cdot 3]\cdot 3 \\  & =14\cdot 10-46\cdot 3 \\  & =46\cdot (-3)+14\cdot 10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=10.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-3)+10=7.
$$
